design.title: Nocturne & Limestone
design.intro: The visual language of Kvittel: midnight navy nights, warm Jerusalem limestone days, aged gold used only as light. Every token and component on this page is the one used in production.

directions.title: Two art directions
directions.body: We explored two directions before committing. Both avoid stock photography and never depict a real tombstone; imagery is typographic, architectural and generated.

a.body: Night-time, intimate and emotional. Deep navy, candle warmth, gold hairlines. Strong for the first moment of arrival; too heavy for long forms and admin work.

b.body: Daylight, editorial and calm. Warm stone textures, navy ink, arched portraits. Excellent legibility for writing and reading; less atmosphere on its own.

directions.chosen: Night for moments of meaning (hero, delivery proof, footer, admin navigation) and limestone for work (writing the kvittel, directory, tracking, admin content). The two alternate like evening and morning, so the journey has rhythm without ever becoming loud.

color.title: Colour
color.body: Gold is an accent, never a fill for large areas. Status colours are earthy (sage, ochre, oxblood, ink) so alerts feel serious rather than alarming. All text pairs meet WCAG AA contrast on their intended surfaces.

type.title: Typography in every script
type.body: Each specimen is rendered with the actual web fonts. Hebrew and Yiddish use Frank Ruhl Libre and Heebo; Latin and Cyrillic use Cormorant Garamond and Manrope. Printed kvittlach use Noto Serif Hebrew and Noto Serif, loaded identically in preview and on the printer.
